subject: Spanska 4
title: Idiomatic expressions and false friends
sourceSummary: Common Spanish idioms, plus classic false friends between Swedish and Spanish, such as "embarazada" and "actualmente".

questions.opener: A classic false friend — the word looks like an English word but means something completely different.
questions.explanation: "Embarazada" means "pregnant", not "embarrassed" (even though it looks like the English word). "Embarrassed" is instead "avergonzado/a" in Spanish.

questions.opener: Another classic case — the word looks like "actually" but means something else.
questions.explanation: "Actualmente" means "currently/at present", not "actually" in the sense of "in fact". "Actually/really" is "en realidad" or "de hecho" in Spanish.

questions.opener: Yet another false friend — the opposite of what you might expect.
questions.explanation: "Sensible" in Spanish means "sensitive" (easily moved, delicate), not "sensible/reasonable" as in English. "Sensible" (reasonable) is "sensato/a" in Spanish.

questions.prompt: What does the expression "costar un ojo de la cara" mean?
questions.opener: A literal translation gives a clue: "to cost an eye from the face".
questions.explanation: "Costar un ojo de la cara" is an idiom meaning "to cost an arm and a leg", comparable to the Swedish expression "kosta skjortan".

questions.prompt: What does the expression "estar en las nubes" mean?
questions.opener: Literally: "to be in the clouds" — what does that correspond to in English?
choices: To be in a good mood
questions.explanation: "Estar en las nubes" means to be absent-minded or daydreaming, similar to the English expression "to have your head in the clouds".

questions.prompt: What does "estoy constipado" mean in Spanish?
questions.opener: A medical false-friend example that often causes embarrassing misunderstandings.
questions.explanation: "Estar constipado" means "to have a cold/stuffy nose" in Spanish, NOT "constipated" as you might think. "Constipated" is "estreñido/a" in Spanish — an important distinction to remember!

questions.prompt: Correct the error: a student writes "Estoy muy embarazada porque dije algo estúpido delante de mi jefe." — what should it say instead?
questions.opener: The student has mixed up a false friend with the word that actually means "embarrassed".
questions.answer: Estoy muy avergonzado/a porque dije algo estúpido delante de mi jefe.
steps: "Embarazada" means "pregnant" in Spanish, not "embarrassed" — a classic example of a false friend with the English word "embarrassed".
The correct word for "embarrassed/ashamed" is "avergonzado" (for a man) or "avergonzada" (for a woman).
The rest of the sentence is correct: "porque dije algo estúpido delante de mi jefe" (because I said something stupid in front of my boss).
Correct sentence: "Estoy muy avergonzado/a porque dije algo estúpido delante de mi jefe."

questions.prompt: What are the most common false friends between Swedish/English and Spanish that you should know at this level?
questions.opener: A list to keep in the back of your mind for the national exam and oral practice.
questions.answer: embarazada = pregnant (NOT embarrassed → avergonzado/a) · actualmente = currently (NOT actually/topical → de hecho/en realidad) · sensible = sensitive (NOT sensible/reasonable → sensato/a) · constipado = has a cold (NOT constipated → estreñido/a) · éxito = success (NOT exit → salida) · largo = long (NOT large → grande) · red = net/network (NOT red → rojo) · pariente = relative (NOT parent → padre/madre) · ropa = clothes (NOT rope → cuerda) · fábrica = factory (NOT fabric → tela). Idioms worth knowing: costar un ojo de la cara (to cost an arm and a leg), estar en las nubes (to be daydreaming), no tener pelos en la lengua (to speak your mind bluntly), tomar el pelo (to tease/pull someone's leg).
